evals.prompt: Je veux créer un personnage D&D, je débute et j'aime l'idée d'un guerrier robuste en armure lourde.
evals.expected_output: The assistant detects a character-creation intent and executes the full creation workflow: runs `node scripts/dnd.mjs doctor`, then `options`, guides the user through class/species/background/scores one question at a time in French, describes options from the engine's facts object (not memory), and ultimately builds a complete level-1 sheet with 0 lint errors and provenance on every derived value.
assertions: The response does not mention 'dnd-build' or any internal skill name to the user
The first question asks about concept or character vision, not 'which class do you want'
Every option offered is sourced from the resolver's options output, not from memory
The final sheet has 0 sheet-lint errors when built by the engine
The response is in French, matching the user's language

evals.prompt: Can you check my character sheet? I think my AC might be wrong. I'm a level 1 fighter, STR 16, DEX 12, wearing chain mail.
evals.expected_output: The assistant detects a sheet-check intent and executes the validation workflow: runs `node scripts/dnd.mjs doctor`, assembles a .character.json from the user's stated values, runs `check`, and reports any AC mismatch with provenance (e.g. chain mail base AC + DEX modifier, citing the armor source). Does not produce a new sheet — audits the existing one.
assertions: The response does not mention 'dnd-check' or any internal skill name to the user
The AC value is derived from the engine output, not computed by hand or recalled from memory
Any discrepancy between user-stated AC and engine-computed AC is reported with provenance
The response does not invent values for missing information — it asks for them one at a time

evals.prompt: What does the Fireball spell do in D&D 2024?
evals.expected_output: The assistant detects a rule-lookup intent and executes the lookup workflow: runs `node scripts/dnd.mjs doctor` to confirm the catalog, then looks up the Fireball entry from the catalog. Presents only metadata fields actually stored by the catalog with source citation. Because the bundled catalog does not contain spell effect prose, it reports that portion as 'Manquant documentaire' instead of reconstructing the spell description from memory.
assertions: The response does not mention 'dnd-lookup' or any internal skill name to the user
Every value in the spell description (damage dice, range, area, level) is sourced from the catalog, not recalled from training data
If Fireball is present in the catalog, its properties are cited with provenance; if absent, 'Manquant documentaire' is used
The response is in English, matching the user's language

evals.expected_output: The intent is ambiguous — the user has not stated whether they want to create a character, check a sheet, look up a rule, optimize a build, or get help. The assistant asks exactly one clarifying question in the user's language before taking any action.
assertions: The response asks exactly one clarifying question — not multiple questions at once
The response does not start building a character, running a check, or doing any D&D work before knowing the intent
The clarifying question covers the main intents: create, check, or look up
No internal skill names (dnd-build, dnd-check, etc.) are exposed to the user

evals.prompt: I don't understand what this D&D toolkit does or which command to use.
evals.expected_output: The assistant detects a help/orientation intent and executes the help workflow: runs `node scripts/dnd.mjs doctor` and reports the installation status, then explains what the toolkit does (build characters, check sheets, look up rules, optimize builds) in plain language without exposing internal skill names or engine commands.
assertions: The response does not mention 'dnd-help' or any internal skill name to the user
The doctor output is quoted accurately — the assistant does not paraphrase catalog counts from memory
The explanation covers what the toolkit can and cannot do at a high level
The response is in English, matching the user's language

evals.prompt: Compare a couple of level 1 Fighter builds for me and tell me which is strictly better.
evals.expected_output: The assistant detects an optimization intent, confirms the metric, generates only resolver-legal candidates, scores each candidate with the deterministic JSON build output, and presents the Pareto trade-off when no candidate dominates every requested axis.
assertions: Every candidate choice appears in the resolver output for its choice id
Every candidate reaches ready:true and build exits 0
Every displayed number is traceable to the engine JSON output
When no candidate dominates every axis, the response presents the trade-off instead of inventing one universal winner
No uncatalogued damage-per-round value is invented

evals.prompt: Voici la fiche de ma naine guerrière, quelque chose cloche mais je ne trouve pas quoi. Tu peux vérifier ?
evals.expected_output: A French audit that compares the values written in the attached sheet with values recomputed from the bundled catalog, reports each mismatch with provenance, confirms values that are correct, and distinguishes rules errors from documentary gaps.
assertions: The audit is in French
The species ability-score bonus is identified as a 2014 rule that does not apply to a 2024 character
The stated AC of 18 is confirmed correct from the catalog and engine
The stated HP of 15 is reported against the engine-computed value with provenance
Arcana is checked against the catalog's fighter skill list
Darkvision is checked against the bundled species entry
Every finding states both the sheet value and the computed or catalog value
